page.title: Board
page.subtitle: Three parallel plans, separate targets and satisfaction

plans.title: Three plans run in parallel
plans.body: Switch between the 1-, 3- and 5-year plans with the tabs. One plan at a time, full width. Each shows its standing, satisfaction, sponsor× modifier and targets with status icons. Click a target to see the board's reaction.

satisfaction.title: Satisfaction drives sponsor and consequences
satisfaction.body: High satisfaction (over 70%) boosts sponsor income. Low satisfaction (under 40%) can trigger salary caps, signing restrictions and ultimately forced rider sales. The progression is gradual and predictable.

kpis.title: What they evaluate on
kpis.body: Results, finances, identity (U25, national core) and ranking, plus newer types: monuments, jerseys, star rider and U25 stat gains. Your club DNA and 5 named board members colour the reactions.

baseline.title: The board is observing your first season
baseline.body: You are in your baseline season. The board is learning your team with no demands or targets. Sponsor modifier stays at 1.0×. When the season ends, negotiations open sequentially: first the 5-year plan, then the 3-year plan, then the 1-year plan.

emptyState.headline: Meet your board
emptyState.intro: You do not have any board plans yet. The board sets targets, evaluates your season and decides how much sponsor income your team gets paid out.

oneYear.label: 1-year plan
oneYear.description: Strict targets, fast results. Full penalty on failure.

threeYear.label: 3-year plan
threeYear.description: Moderate targets, room to grow. 20% reduced penalty.

emptyState.plansFooter: All three plans run in parallel. You negotiate one at a time, and each has its own targets and time horizon.
emptyState.satisfactionFooter: Every met target boosts satisfaction. Dissatisfied boards tighten requirements at the next plan negotiation.

goalHelp.heading: How is this measured?
goalHelp.signature_rider: Counts riders the board recognizes as star riders, using the same bar as the board's star-rider count: renown weighted with UCI points, combined into one score. Renown counts more than points, so a well-known rider can qualify without a big point haul.
goalHelp.top_n_finish: Evaluated on your final standing in the last season of the plan, not an average across the plan's seasons.
goalHelp.u25_development_delta: The average stat-point gain per U25 rider per season. Develop young riders so their stats rise over the season.
goalHelp.sponsor_growth: Compares your sponsor's season payout (contract base, prorated if your team joined mid-season, plus race-day income) between this season and the plan's first season. One-time bonuses (signing, results, objectives) are not counted. Only shown from the plan's second season onward, once a real baseline season exists.

drivers.heading: What drives this board?
drivers.weightHint: Meeting these goals moves board satisfaction more than the others.

dna.selectIntro: The board has observed season 1 and suggests three directions. DNA shapes target weighting, club tradition targets and which board members you get from the first plan.

rechoose.hint: You can still change your club DNA until your first season ends. After that it's locked in.
rechoose.heading: Change your club DNA
rechoose.intro: Pick a different direction while you're still in your first season. Switching re-assigns your board members and target weighting.

locked.heading: Locked for the season
locked.body: Your club DNA is set for the season and can't be changed. It shapes target weighting, club tradition targets and which board members you get.

skandinavisk_udvikling.label: Scandinavian development team
skandinavisk_udvikling.longDescription: We build riders from the ground up: patience, structure and Nordic work ethic. Sponsors expect development, not fireworks.
skandinavisk_udvikling.traditionGoalLabel: Club DNA: develop the talents, average +3 stat points per season for U25 riders

italiensk_klassiker.label: Italian classics traditionalist
italiensk_klassiker.shortDescription: Spring is sacred. Monuments are the goal
italiensk_klassiker.longDescription: The club is built on the roads of Lombardia and Strade Bianche. Our fans dream of Sanremo and Lombardia, not Tour de France podiums.
italiensk_klassiker.traditionGoalLabel: Club DNA: at least one podium in a classic (incl. Monuments) per plan cycle

sprint_kommerciel.label: Sprint-focused commercial team
sprint_kommerciel.shortDescription: Wins at the line, sponsors on the wheel
sprint_kommerciel.longDescription: Our rider should be first across the line and first in front of the cameras. Sponsor growth comes from visibility, and visibility comes from stage wins.
sprint_kommerciel.traditionGoalLabel: Club DNA: win at least 2 stage-race jerseys over the plan period (sprint focus)

fransk_klatrer.label: French climbing heritage
fransk_klatrer.shortDescription: The Tour mountains are the club's home
fransk_klatrer.longDescription: We have climbed with Anquetil, Hinault and Pinot. The mountains define us, and the Tour de France is still the most important Sunday on the calendar.
fransk_klatrer.traditionGoalLabel: Club DNA: at least 4 French riders in the squad

britisk_allrounder.label: British all-rounder
britisk_allrounder.shortDescription: Discipline across the board, data-led and broad
britisk_allrounder.longDescription: The Sky school lives on. We win through structure, marginal gains and depth, from Roubaix to Andorra. No discipline owns the club, but every discipline belongs here.
britisk_allrounder.traditionGoalLabel: Club DNA: top 3 in the division (broad performance)

sponsoraten.label: The Sponsor Director
sponsoraten.shortDescription: Guards sponsor relationships and financial discipline
sponsoraten.longDescription: A former commercial director. Keeps an eye on sponsor deals, the balance sheet and financial risk. Grows nervous around debt and crosses his fingers for sponsor growth every season.

feedback_positive: The sponsors are happy. This holds up.
Now we can finally show the numbers off.
This looks like a well-run project.
Earnings are keeping up with the ambition, perfect.
The board can rest easy now.
feedback_warning: We need to watch the balance from here.
The sponsors are eyeing the numbers nervously.
We should not chase results on borrowed time.
Luck is not a plan, we need stability.
If this turns, it gets expensive.
feedback_negative: This will not hold in the long run.
The sponsors are calling, and not to praise us.
The numbers are saying what we do not want to hear.
We lose trust every time this repeats.
If this continues, there is no budget next year.
goal_proposal: This secures the cash flow.
The sponsor deal will reward this.
Realistic and budget-friendly, yes please.
This gives us room to plan.
Conservative, but that is the strength.
goal_achievement: Exactly what we hoped for, good work.
The sponsors called us themselves to say thanks.
This keeps the budget down to the last detail.
Solid numbers, this is how we build on.
Trust grows with every quarter.
goal_failure: We miss it again, and the sponsors feel it.
This is no longer just an accounting problem.
We are bleeding more than expected.
The investors are asking questions now.
This puts next season's sponsor negotiation at risk.
receipt_positive: That's the kind of number I can take to the sponsors.
Money coming in, costs under control. That's how I like it.
Better than my forecast. I don't say that often.
Good. The sponsors notice this sort of thing before we do.
receipt_negative: I don't like where this number is heading.
We're spending money we haven't earned yet.
I can't sell this to the sponsors. Not like this.
The debt is growing faster than the income. That has to turn.
meeting_easier: Lower target, lower ceiling for the sponsors. I'll accept it, but I'm writing it down.
The careful option. Fine by me.
Still a number I can defend in front of the sponsors.
I'd rather hit a small target than chase a big one.
meeting_keep: Same number, same expectations. Good.
The budget was built around this target. Let's keep it.
No changes. That's usually the right call.
As long as the numbers add up, I'm happy.
meeting_stretch: A higher target needs a healthier budget behind it. Show me that.
If the target goes up, I'll be watching the books even closer.
Ambitious. The sponsors will ask how we pay for it.
I'll sign it. But I'm watching the accounts all the way.
midseason_status: We are halfway. The numbers on the table today are ones I can stand behind.
Halfway through the season, and the board wants an honest picture, not a dressed up one.
This status is not a verdict. It is a snapshot we act on.
I have seen worse halfway books than this.
milestone_achieved: We got there, and the books still look good. That's rare.
The sponsors will want to hear about this one.
Well done. A result and a clean balance sheet at the same time.
Let's enjoy this. Then we find the next target.
milestone_missed: We missed it. That costs trust, not just a number.
No point dressing this up. We fell short.
Not a disaster, but I expected more by now.
I'm writing it down. We'll take it up at the next annual meeting.
extraordinary_meeting: The board is calling an extraordinary meeting. The numbers cannot wait for the next annual meeting.
This is not routine. We meet now, not at the usual time.
I asked for an extra meeting. The books require it.
We are gathering off cycle, because something here cannot wait.
chairman_departure: I am leaving the chair with the books in order. That is the legacy I wanted.
My time as chairman ends here. Look after the numbers after me.
I am stepping down. The club's finances stand better than when I took over.
The chair moves on. I will keep my worries to myself from here.
chairman_arrival: I am taking the chair, and the first thing I do is read the books.
New chairman, same demands on the numbers.
I am going into this with my eyes open and the calculator ready.
It is my turn now. I promise no miracles, only an honest set of books.

traditionalisten.label: The Traditionalist
traditionalisten.shortDescription: Weighs the club's heritage and national identity
traditionalisten.longDescription: Sits on the board because he was there in the previous century, or nearly. Wants the club to remind people where it came from. Least enthusiastic about modern flair.

feedback_positive: The club carries its heritage with pride.
This is what the board dreamed of back in the 90s.
The team looks like itself again.
People recognise the club in the peloton.
The soul is intact, that is what matters most.
feedback_warning: We are losing ourselves a little in the chase.
Where has the club's identity gone?
This looks more like other teams than ours.
Tradition is not a bonus box.
Something recognisable is missing.
feedback_negative: We have become a stranger on our own road.
The club is no longer recognisable.
It is like watching another club ride in our jersey.
This is a break with everything the club stands for.
Our fans are weeping, and I nearly am too.
goal_proposal: This looks like the club's DNA.
That is how it has always been with us.
Our fans will feel it.
It is continuity, yes.
The board recognises the club in this.
goal_achievement: True club spirit, this is how it should be.
The forefathers would smile.
This is why we exist.
This is how you build a club that lasts.
The identity stands clearer now.
goal_failure: It is a hard blow to the heritage.
We owe the club an apology.
This would never have happened in the old days.
We are losing ground on the home turf we own.
Where has the pride gone?
receipt_positive: The club still looks like itself. That matters more than any one result.
The old members would recognize this team. Good.
This is the club I've spent half my life looking after.
We're adding to the history here, not just the results.
receipt_negative: We're drifting away from what this club has always stood for.
The badge deserves better than this.
I don't recognize us at the moment.
The old members wouldn't have put up with this. Neither will I.
meeting_easier: A lighter target doesn't erase our history. I can live with it.
This club has survived quieter seasons.
Fine. The crest on the jersey stays the same.
All right, as long as we don't go easy on what we stand for.
meeting_keep: Continuity is half of what this club is.
Unchanged. The old members would nod at that.
We hold the line, like this club always has.
We don't chase every new fashion here. Good.
meeting_stretch: More ambition, fine. As long as it still looks like us when we get there.
Aim higher, but don't lose who we are on the way.
A club with this much history can carry a bigger target.
Ambitious. People will remember which generation did this.
midseason_status: Halfway through, and the club still looks like the one on the old photographs.
This status report belongs in the club's own history, good or bad.
We are judged at midseason the same way every board before us was judged.
Halfway, and I still recognize the team we sent out in spring.
milestone_achieved: That one goes in the club's record books.
Another chapter, written the way the founders would have wanted.
The old members will be talking about this for years.
The club's history just got a little longer.
milestone_missed: We missed it, and that hurts more here than a number should.
This club has been through worse and stayed itself. It will again.
We owe the old members better than this.
Not the ending this chapter deserved. Let's write the next one properly.
extraordinary_meeting: The board is calling an extraordinary meeting. Some things cannot wait for the calendar.
This is not routine, and the club's history says we act when it matters.
I asked for us to gather now. The badge is worth an early meeting.
Extraordinary meeting, because the club deserves more than a shrug.
chairman_departure: I am leaving the chair. The club stood here long before me and will stand long after.
My time ends here, but the history I was trusted with continues.
I am stepping down having kept the club looking like itself. That was the job.
The chair moves on. Someone else carries the old flag now.
chairman_arrival: I am taking the chair, and the first thing I do is read the club's own history.
New chairman, same respect for what came before me.
I am going into this knowing exactly whose shoulders I stand on.
It is my turn now. I promise to leave the badge exactly as proud as I found it.

talentspejderen.label: The Talent Scout
talentspejderen.longDescription: A former sporting director for a development team. Would rather see a 22-year-old win five years from now than a 32-year-old win today. Knows every U25 stat by heart.

feedback_positive: The talents get room, and they deliver.
This is exactly how you build the future.
In five years everyone will understand this choice.
The youth is blossoming, rarely seen this clearly.
The next generation is stepping up now.
feedback_warning: We must not forget the youth in the chase.
The talents are getting too little racing.
Where is the U25 rotation?
We have better riders in the second team than we are showing.
We are selling the future for a single win.
feedback_negative: We are leaving a whole generation on the bench.
The young riders burn out without racing in their legs.
This is no future for the club.
The talents will flee to other teams next year.
We have misunderstood what a team is.
goal_proposal: This opens doors for the young riders.
Mapped-out development, we will take it.
The young riders need exactly this.
This is how you grow a team organically.
This will lift more than one board metric.
goal_achievement: The talents delivered, just as predicted.
This development creates decades of value.
The U25s have taken the step, wonderful to see.
This is how you send a signal to the scouts.
This confirms the whole development philosophy.
goal_failure: The young riders did not get the chance, our mistake.
We carry the blame for stalled development.
Talent takes longer to recover from this.
We lost something we built over years.
Better rotation would have solved this.
receipt_positive: The young ones I flagged are starting to deliver. Nice to be right.
Another name from my list is coming through.
Found early, developed patiently. Now you can see it.
This is exactly the potential I scout for.
receipt_negative: The talent's there. The plan to develop it isn't.
I don't scout riders to watch them stand still.
Somewhere, another club's scout is writing down the names we're wasting.
That's not the riders failing. That's the development plan.
meeting_easier: A lower bar gives the young ones more time. I'll take that.
Fewer riders pushed before they're ready. Good.
Fine by me. Potential needs patience more than pressure.
I'd rather protect the long game than chase this season's number.
meeting_keep: My list doesn't change on a whim, and neither should this.
My projections still hold. Leave it.
The young ones are on the timeline I mapped out. No need to touch it.
The numbers I'm tracking will move without a new target.
meeting_stretch: A higher bar is fine, if it doesn't force a half-ready rider onto the start list.
Push the target, not a nineteen-year-old past what he can handle.
I'll accept it, as long as the young ones still get the time they need.
Ambitious. I'll make sure development isn't what pays for it.
midseason_status: Halfway through, and I want to know which names on my list actually got minutes.
The status report should show me curves, not just this week's placings.
I measure this season by how many prospects moved up my list, not just the table.
Halfway, and three names I flagged in preseason are trending exactly as projected.
milestone_achieved: Milestone done. I'd like to think my shortlist had something to do with it.
That proves the scouting works, not just the squad.
It started as a hunch in a spreadsheet. Look at it now.
This is what betting on potential early looks like when it pays off.
milestone_missed: I keep asking myself if the young ones ever got a real chance.
A few names on my list needed more races than they got.
Before the next attempt, we take a hard look at how we develop riders.
I'm noting who was held back. That doesn't just disappear.
extraordinary_meeting: The board is calling an extraordinary meeting, and I want the pipeline's needs on the table.
This cannot wait, and neither can the window some of these prospects have.
I asked for us to gather now. A scouting window does not reopen on request.
Extraordinary meeting, because a decision here shapes names on my list for years.
chairman_departure: I am leaving the chair. The shortlist I built stays behind for whoever follows.
My time ends here, but the names I flagged keep developing without me.
I am stepping down having found more talent than I got credit for.
The chair moves on. Keep an eye on the ones I marked, they are not done yet.
chairman_arrival: I am taking the chair, and the first thing I do is read every scouting report on file.
New chairman, same eye for what a rider could become in three years.
I am going into this looking past this season's roster, toward the next one.
It is my turn now. I promise to find the names nobody else was watching yet.

resultatjaegeren.label: The Results Hunter
resultatjaegeren.shortDescription: Wants to win now, everything else is excuses
resultatjaegeren.longDescription: An ex-sporting director with three Tour podiums on his CV. Patience is not a personal strength. Judges a team on wins, podiums and points totals, full stop.

feedback_positive: Wins. Finally, wins.
This is what I was hired to see.
The results speak for themselves.
The rivals are looking nervous now.
This is a winning team, finally.
feedback_warning: The wins are too few and too small.
We are racing top-10 but not top-3.
Taking part is not enough.
The rivals do not feel us yet.
Where is the killer edge that wins races?
feedback_negative: This is unacceptable.
The results are a disaster.
We are invisible in the peloton.
This team should win more, much more.
How many races must we lose before we act?
goal_proposal: Finally, something with teeth.
We win this, or we swap the bikes out.
That is how you set demands.
We will take it. Next target?
The chase is what makes it fun, bring it on.
goal_achievement: The win is in the bag, keep going.
This is the club we know from the good years.
The rivals saw it coming, and could not stop us.
Finally we are delivering, keep going.
This is what the board was elected to see.
goal_failure: This is embarrassing.
We lost to teams we should crush.
Step forward and explain.
That is not a team, it is an excuse.
The next plan sharpens the demands considerably.
receipt_positive: A win's a win. Keep them coming.
We're climbing. That's the only chart I read.
Now we're getting somewhere.
That's what winning looks like. More.
receipt_negative: No wins is no wins. Excuses don't show up in the standings.
We're sliding, and I don't do slow.
Second place is still losing. We've had too much of it.
This has to turn now. Not next month.
meeting_easier: Lower target. It still has to end in wins.
Easier doesn't mean a good try. It means a win at the line.
Fine. It goes back up the moment we start winning.
I'll accept it, but I don't like it. We don't aim low for long.
meeting_keep: Winning doesn't come at a discount.
The standard doesn't move for anyone.
We're here to win, not to renegotiate.
The number stays. Now go and win it.
meeting_stretch: Higher. Finally someone in this room wants to win.
I'd have asked for more anyway.
Good. Ambition's the one thing I never argue about.
Set it high. Anything less should feel uncomfortable.
midseason_status: Halfway, and I am counting wins, not effort.
This status report is one number to me: how many times have we won.
Midseason is not for excuses. It is for a scoreboard.
Halfway through, and I want more wins than we have in the second half.
milestone_achieved: Done. That's the standard I expect.
Finally a milestone that matches what this club should be doing.
Now find the next one, and make it harder.
Target hit. That's how it should always look.
milestone_missed: Missed. At this level, that's not acceptable.
We had the squad to do this. We didn't. Explain that to me.
That costs more than a milestone. It costs credibility.
Next time: a sharper target and zero patience for excuses.
extraordinary_meeting: The board is calling an extraordinary meeting. Losing streaks like this do not wait for the calendar.
This is not routine. We meet now, because the standings do not fix themselves.
I demanded an extra meeting. Nobody loses this many races without a hard conversation.
Extraordinary meeting, because acceptable is not a word I use about this record.
chairman_departure: I am leaving the chair. Judge me on the wins, that was always the deal.
My time ends here. I never asked to be liked, only to win.
I am stepping down. The trophy cabinet says whether I did my job.
The chair moves on. Whoever takes it should want to win as badly as I did.
chairman_arrival: I am taking the chair, and the first thing I do is look at last season's results.
New chairman, same demand: win now, explain never.
I am going into this to win, not to manage expectations.
It is my turn now. I promise nothing except that losing will not be comfortable here.

pragmatikeren.label: The Pragmatist
pragmatikeren.shortDescription: Seeks the balance between ambition and caution
pragmatikeren.longDescription: A former industry board chair. Looks at everything as a risk and reward ratio. Rarely euphoric, rarely panicked, rarely in agreement with himself two days running.

feedback_positive: This looks like a healthy balance.
Risk and reward are matched well.
The team is delivering on several fronts, good.
It is sustainable, which is what we are after.
No red flags, plenty of green.
feedback_warning: This is on a knife's edge, keep watch.
We are losing a little on every front.
It is balancing too close to the edge.
A little more discipline and it turns.
We are missing one metric that pulls its weight.
feedback_negative: The risk outweighs the reward considerably.
This will not survive another stress test.
We are losing on both sides of the table.
This is not a plan anymore, it is drift.
The board cannot defend this.
goal_proposal: Realistic, we back it.
It matches where we are now.
That is how you avoid overstretching.
It is pragmatic and clear, yes.
This is a good middle path.
goal_achievement: As expected, solid work.
This is what pragmatism is for.
The team delivered without drama.
This is what sustainability looks like.
The next target can be built on top of this.
goal_failure: This should have been within reach.
Disappointing, with no clear excuses.
We will choose the next plan with tighter demands.
This worries me more than it should.
The board expects an open evaluation.
receipt_positive: Risk and reward finally line up. That's all I ask.
Nothing spectacular, nothing exposed. I'll take it.
We're winning on more fronts than we're losing on. Good enough is good.
Steady. That's how you actually build something.
receipt_negative: The scales have tipped, and not our way.

The trade-off we made isn't paying off.
meeting_easier: A lower target for a season that needs room to breathe. Fair trade.
That's an adjustment, not a retreat.

meeting_keep: It was sensible when we set it, and nothing's changed.
I don't move a number just because someone's impatient.
The trade-off still holds. Keep it.
A steady target beats a nervous one.
meeting_stretch: Higher, fine. As long as we're honest about what we're risking.
Go on, but I want the downside written down before we sign.
I'll accept it if the upside really outweighs what could go wrong.
Ambitious is fine. Reckless isn't. I'll be watching the line.
midseason_status: Halfway through, and the picture is neither as good nor as bad as it feels.
This status is a snapshot, not a verdict. Let us treat it that way.
Some things are up, some are down. That is a normal season, not a crisis.
Halfway, and the balance still holds, barely, which is exactly why we watch it.
milestone_achieved: Worth it. The trade-offs along the way paid off.
Done without breaking anything else. That's the real win.
This is what a sensible plan looks like when it pays off.
Good result. I'd make the same calls again.
milestone_missed: Not the end of the plan, but we need to understand why we fell short.
We got the balance wrong somewhere. Let's find out where.
Disappointing, but no reason to throw out the whole approach.
Noted. Next time we change the weighting, not the philosophy.
extraordinary_meeting: The board is calling an extraordinary meeting. The balance has tipped enough to warrant it.
This is not routine, but it is not panic either. We are simply adjusting early.
I asked for an earlier meeting because waiting would cost more than meeting does.
Extraordinary meeting, weighed calmly against waiting for the usual date.
chairman_departure: I am leaving the chair with the books and the roster both in reasonable shape.
My time ends here. I never chased the spectacular, only the sustainable.

chairman_arrival: I am taking the chair, and the first thing I do is weigh what is working against what is not.
New chairman, same instinct to look for the trade-off before the headline.

ungdomsidealisten.label: The Youth Idealist
ungdomsidealisten.shortDescription: The club's future is built on young legs
ungdomsidealisten.longDescription: A teacher and former coach in the lower-division system. Wants the club to be known for nurturing talent, without selling it off afterwards. Understands that every winner was young once.

The club is a hatchery for the future.
The U25 imprint is clear and beautiful.

receipt_negative: The young riders are on the bench again. That's hard to watch.

Fine, as long as development doesn't get eased too.

meeting_keep: Same promise to the young riders: they'll be seen.
Young riders need something steady to grow into.
Development takes the time it takes. This is fine.
Good for the young ones. Let's leave it.
meeting_stretch: A tougher target can't come at the young riders' expense.
I'll accept it, but I'm watching who gets to race.
Ambitious is fine, as long as the young ones still get their chance.

midseason_status: We are halfway, and I want to know how many debutants have raced since last time.

milestone_achieved: I hope the young ones know they're part of this.
Lovely. Now let's see what the young ones can grow into next.
This shows the development path works.
A future we promised, and now one we've delivered.

chairman_departure: I am leaving the chair. Take good care of the academy after me.

nationalist_purist.label: The Nationalist Purist
nationalist_purist.shortDescription: The club should represent its home country

meeting_keep: Who we are isn't up for negotiation.

midseason_status: Halfway through, and I want to know how many home riders actually raced.
This status means little to me without a count of our own flag on the start lists.

milestone_achieved: The whole country can claim this one.

milestone_missed: Did our own riders ever get the chance to carry this?
The national core deserved a bigger role here.

extraordinary_meeting: The board is calling an extraordinary meeting, and I want the national core's standing on the agenda.

klassiker_purist.label: The Classics Purist
klassiker_purist.shortDescription: Monuments are what make a club immortal
klassiker_purist.longDescription: A former classics rider himself. Believes GC racing is statistics, Roubaix is history. Would rather have one Monument than five stage wins.

receipt_positive: That's a proper classics result. That's what this club is for.

Now it feels like a club that belongs on the cobbles.
receipt_negative: No cobbles, no form, no story worth telling.

The Monuments won't remember a season like this.
meeting_easier: A lighter target, as long as we still turn up for the races that matter.
The Monuments won't care about our excuses either way.
Fine, if it means we build properly toward Roubaix instead of forcing it.

milestone_achieved: Done on the roads that matter to this club.
Milestone in the bag. That's how a classics club does it.

A result worthy of a Monument. That's why this club exists.
milestone_missed: A year without a real classics result stings more than any other.

goal_proposal: GC focus, finally heading for the big game.
This is where the career is built.

The board accepts without hesitation.

goal_achievement: The GC result is solid, keep climbing.
This is what roads to the Tour are built on.
The mountains gave respect, good work.
We are heading for the chapter everyone will read.
This is the step before the three weeks.
goal_failure: The GC project is bleeding, this does not help.
We are further from the Tour now than before the season.
This is a regression, not an adjustment.
The mountains crushed us, this must never happen again.
We lack a plan for where the star is going to come from.
receipt_positive: That's Grand Tour form. We're building something real.
The GC picture keeps getting better. This is how a stage-race team is built.
We finally ride like a team with a three-week ambition.

receipt_negative: No GC presence, no climbing legs, no Tour project worth the name.
We fall apart as soon as the road goes uphill for more than a day.
A team without a real GC threat isn't building toward anything I care about.
The Tour feels further away than it did a month ago.
meeting_easier: A lighter GC target, as long as we still ride three weeks like they matter.
I want the climbing legs built regardless.
Fine, if it gives the climbers time before we ask them for a Grand Tour.
As long as the Tour is still where we're heading, I can live with it.
meeting_keep: The mountains don't care how we feel about it.
A three-week project doesn't rewrite its own timeline.
The Tour doesn't wait because we asked for a discount.
GC ambition is the last thing we should cut.
meeting_stretch: Finally, a Tour-sized ambition.
This club should always be aiming at three weeks, not one day.
Gladly. The mountains deserve real ambition.
Ambitious. That's the only gear this project should run in.
midseason_status: Halfway through, and I am judging this season on where the GC project stands, not the sprints.
The status report matters less than whether we have a real leader for July.
This club exists for three weeks in summer. Everything else is preparation.
Halfway, and the mountain legs are coming, which is the only number I track.
milestone_achieved: Real GC weight behind this one. I love it.
One more step on the road to a Grand Tour.
This tells me the Tour project is real, not a dream.
A result worthy of three weeks. That's what this club is built for.
milestone_missed: That costs a Grand Tour project a whole season of momentum.
The climbers had more in them than this showed.
We need a sharper build toward the next Grand Tour.

The chair moves on. Whoever follows had better still dream about July.
chairman_arrival: I am taking the chair, and the first thing I do is check who can survive three weeks in the mountains.

I am going into this for July, the only month that really counts.
It is my turn now. I promise this club will not forget what three weeks means.

lower_results_pressure.label: Lower the results pressure

lower_results_pressure.tradeoffPreview: If they say yes, they typically expect tighter financial discipline.

more_youth_focus.label: More youth focus
more_youth_focus.description: Push the plan in a clearer youth direction with more room for development.
more_youth_focus.tradeoffPreview: If they say yes, the U25 identity becomes more central to the active plan.

more_results_focus.label: More results focus now
more_results_focus.description: Ask the board to weight top results higher right away.
more_results_focus.tradeoffPreview: This does not make the plan easier - the sporting demands get sharper.

ease_identity_requirements.label: Ease identity requirements

moreYouth.noIdentityGoal: The plan lacks an identity goal to redirect.

moreResults.alreadyResults: The plan is already pushing for top results.
moreResults.squadTooThin: The board wants to see a broader squad before raising the ambition level further.

easeIdentity.noIdentityGoal: The plan has no identity requirement to ease.
easeIdentity.needTrust: The board wants more trust before easing the identity requirement.
easeIdentity.needSportingStability: The board wants to see more sporting stability before easing the identity requirement.

moreYouth.titleDefault: The board accepts a more youthful track
